🚨 A Perfect Burglary: Antonello da Messina’s Works Were Stolen


Four of the most important works of art by the 15th-century Renaissance master Antonello da Messina were stolen during a national holiday from a museum in the Sicilian port city of Messina.

Thieves gained access to the regional museum of Messina, or MuMe, on Saturday evening, possibly capitalising on attention being focused on La Vara, a huge religious festival that takes place in the city on 15 August, when Italy marks the ferragosto national holiday.

Bypassing the alarm systems, the gang broke into a security display box and stole four wood panels painted by Antonello.

Thieves took three of the five surviving panels that made up an altarpiece known as the Polittico di San Gregorio, one of the Sicilian painter’s most important works.

Originally composed of six panels created for the Monastero di San Gregorio, which was destroyed in the 1908 Messina earthquake, the altarpiece was the only work by the Sicilian painter never to have left his home city.

A fourth work was taken from a secure display case: a small double-sided painting depicting the Virgin and Child with a Franciscan monk on one side and Christ on the other.

The painting had belonged to the Wilhelm Soldan collection and was sold by Christie’s to the Sicilian regional government in 2003, the year it was attributed to Antonello.

Born around ​1430, Antonello trained in Naples where he studied the works of Provençal and Flemish artists, whose influence is apparent in his works.

In February, the Italian government secured a rare Antonello masterpiece at auction in New York, spending $14.9m on his Ecce Homo. The painting, sold at Sotheby’s, is an intensely human portrait of the suffering Christ, believed to have been completed about 1460.

The theft took place after Italian police on Friday had recovered three paintings by the French masters Paul Cézanne, Pierre-Auguste Renoir and Henri Matisse that were stolen earlier this year from a private museum near the northern city of Parma.

Wall Street is pricing Anthropic on 2028, not 2026. 🤖

Anthropic is preparing for what could become one of the largest IPOs ever.

But according to Reuters, investors are looking unusually far into the future to decide what the AI company might be worth.

The key number: $190–200 billion.

That is the revenue Anthropic is reportedly projecting for 2028, compared with a revenue run rate of more than $47 billion reported in May. (Reuters⁠)

Why does that matter?

Normally, mature companies are valued heavily on earnings and cash flow.

But frontier AI companies are still spending enormous amounts on:

• GPUs
• inference
• model training
• computing capacity
• talent

So investors are increasingly asking a different question:

Not “How profitable is this company today?”

But:

“What could its economics look like once the infrastructure is built and the business reaches scale?” 📊

That makes AI valuation unusually dependent on assumptions about the future.

Revenue has to keep growing.

Compute has to become more efficient.

And costs need to grow slower than the business itself.

The AI race is no longer only about building the best model.

It is also becoming a test of whether extraordinary technological growth can eventually turn into extraordinary financial performance.

Homemade Soft Pretzels 

Recipe Ingredients

For the Dough:
4 cups all-purpose flour
1 ½ cups warm water
1 TBS sugar
2 tsp salt
4 TBS butter, melted
2.5 tsp instant yeast

For the Baking Soda Water Bath:
2.5 qts water
2/3 cup baking soda

For the Topping:
Egg wash (1 egg, scrambled)
Pretzel salt or coarse sea salt

Instructions

Make the Dough: 
Mix the warm water, sugar, and instant yeast in a large bowl. Add the flour, salt, and melted butter. Knead until a smooth dough forms, then let it rest or rise as preferred. Divide and shape into 6 pretzels.

Prepare the Bath: 
Bring the 2.5 quarts of water and 2/3 cup of baking soda to a rolling boil in a large pot.

Boil the Pretzels:
Drop each shaped pretzel into the boiling water bath for 30 seconds. 

Remove with a slotted spatula and place onto a lined baking sheet.

First Bake: 
Brush the pretzels with the first layer of scrambled egg wash. Bake at 450°F for 6 minutes.

Second Bake: 
Remove from the oven. Apply a second layer of egg wash and sprinkle generously with the coarse sea salt. Return to the oven and bake for an additional 6 minutes until golden brown.
